answer: Credit-bureau nullifiers: at signup, an identity runs a soft inquiry with a licensed credit bureau, which returns only a salted hash of the person's file, never the details. The registry rejects any hash it has already seen, so each person maps to one seat. A farm needs a distinct, real credit history per identity; buying stolen files leaves an echo of fraud alerts, and synthetic files take years to age. No sock puppet finds a safe haven in an ocean of fakes. Limitation: people without credit files, common in many countries, are shut out and need another path.
